REPLY TO POINTS REAISED IN THE QUESTIONNAIRE ON COIR BOARD SERVICES (CLASSIFICATION, CONTROL &
APPEAL) BYE LAWS, 1969.
1. Point referred- Whether the bye-laws have been laid on the tale of each House of Parliament. If so the details in this regard.
Reply to Point No. 1:-
As per Section 27 (4) of the Coir Industry Act, 1953 (45 of 1953), every Bye-law made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in session, for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or
more successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session immediately following the session or the successive session aforesaid.
The Section 27 (4) was inserted in the Coir Industry Act based on the Delegated Legislation’s Provisions (Amendment) Act, 1986. Before 1986, it
was required only to notify the Bye-law made/amended in the official Gazette by the Central Government in terms of Section 27 (2) and (3) of the
Coir Industry Act, However, since 1986, every Bye-law made under the Act will have to be laid before each House of Parliament as contemplated
in Section 27 (4). Records are being collected to confirm and get the dates of placement of these Bye-laws o the Table of both the Houses of
Parliament.
2. Point referred- Bye-laws 3-Application
These Bye-laws shall apply to every employee of the Board, but shall not apply to:
a. any person in casual employment;
 
b. any person on daily wages:
c. any person subject to discharge from service on less than one months notice;
2. Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (1) the Central Government may by order exclude from the operation of all or any of these
Bye-laws any class of employees of the Board.
3. If any doubt arises as to whether these Bye-laws or any of them apply to any person, the matter shall be forwarded to the Central
Government who shall decide the same.
The non-applicability of bye-laws to any person subject to discharge from service on less than one months notice; as prescribed in bye-laws (c)
above, excluding from the operation of all or any of these bye-laws any class of employees of the Board, mentioned in sub bye-law (2) above and in
case of doubt, as to whether the bye laws or any of them apply to any person, the matter shall be referred to the Central Government who shall
decide as contained in sub bye-law (3) above give a contention to a reader that bye-laws do not apply in general and discriminate among its
employees. Why don’t the Board abolish all the three sub-bye-laws?
Is there any objection to make applicability of bye-laws crystal clear by the Ministry as envisaged in the Central Civil Services (Classification,
Control & Appeal) Rules, 1957 (now 1965) for the persons to whom they will be applicable?
Reply to Point No. 2
There is no discrimination amongst the employees of the Board. The disciplinary proceedings as applicable to regular employees are not applicable
to the Casual employees, daily wagers etc. even under CCS (CCA) Rules. However, the Board will be guided by the recommendations of this
Committee on Subordinate Legislation.

COMMENTS TO QUESTIONNAIRE OF THE COMMITTEE ON SUBORDINATE LEGISLATION, RAJYA SABHA TO EXAMINE
RUBBER BOARD SERVICE RULES 1961
Question No. 1 Whether the rules have been laid on the table of each house of Parliament? If so the details in this regard.
Comments Section 25 (3) of the Rubber Act 1947 (XXIV) of 1947 prescribes that every rule made on matters listed under Section 25 of the Act
shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made before each house of Parliament. The Rubber Board (Service) Rules, 1961 were made in the year
1961 and published on 23rd May, 1961. Records of that period are not available.
Question No. 2 Rule 2 (c)
‘Board’s employee’ means any person employed under the Board other than the Chairman, the Officers appointed under Section 6A of the Rubber
Act, 1947 and the Government Officers lent to the Board.
Why the Chairman and the Officers appointed under Section 6A of the Rubber Act are not treated as Board employee? Kindly explain.
Comments Rule 2 (c) of the Rubber Board (Service) Rules, 1961 are applicable to employees of the Rubber Board excepting for the Chairman and
Officers mentioned in Section 6A of the Rubber Act. There is specific provision in the Rubber Act and Rubber Rules with regard to the appointment
of the Chairman and the Executive Officers appointed under Section 6A.
Under Section 6A of the Rubber Act, the Chairman will be appointed by the Central Government. His terms and functions are also prescribed in the
Rubber Act and Rubber Rules.
The Executive Officers appointed under 6A of the Rubber Act are Rubber production Commissioner and the Secretary. Their terms of appointment
and functions are also specified in the Rubber Act and Rubber Rules. The Central Government makes appointments to these posts. In respect of
Rubber Production Commissioner and Secretary the Government usually stipulates that the terms and conditions of the service will be on par with
the employees of similar grade in the Rubber Board.
Therefore, Chairman and Officers appointed under 6A of the Rubber Act are not governed by the Rubber Board (Service) Rules, 1961.

a. Under rule 5 (a) there appears to be no justification in disqualifying a woman from appointment in service if her marriage takes place
without the knowledge that the person with whom she is married already has living wife. Is there any objection in exempting such person by
inserting an appropriate saving provision.
b. Under the proviso what could be the other ground for exempting any person from the operation of this rule? Does it include personal law
which in certain cases permits second marriage? What are the comments of the Ministry in this regard.
Comments Rule 5 restricts appointment to the Board’s service only from persons of monogamous marriage. However, there is no objection to
inserting an appropriate saving provision under rule 5 (a) providing for appointment of a woman married to a man without her knowledge of his
having already a living wife. However the proviso to Rule 5, enabling Government to give exemption on special grounds can be used for avoiding
hardship in such cases.
On the above issue the Board would like to be guided by the valuable opinion of the Committee. However as per Central Civil Services (Conduct)

A person whose age exceeds 25 years may not ordinarily be appointed to the service by direct recruitment.

prescribed is for recruitment to base level posts, the qualification of which does not go beyond graduation and which does not require previous
experience. There are many higher posts to which promotion is not the channel of recruitment. These have to be filled up by direct recruitment and
the age limit is suitably prescribed in the recruitment rules. Forego for Group B posts upto the level of Rs. 6500-10500 the age limit is 35 years, for
Group A posts upto the level of Rs. 10000-15200, the age limit is 40 years and for still higher posts in Group A the age limit is 45 years.

1. Point referred- Whether the bye-laws have been laid on the tale of each House of Parliament. If so the details in this regard.
Reply to Point No. 1:-
As per Section 27 (4) of the Coir Industry Act, 1953 (45 of 1953), every Bye-law made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in session, for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or
more successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session immediately following the session or the successive session aforesaid.
The Section 27 (4) was inserted in the Coir Industry Act based on the Delegated Legislation’s Provisions (Amendment) Act, 1986. Before 1986, it
was required only to notify the Bye-law made/amended in the official Gazette by the Central Government in terms of Section 27 (2) and (3) of the
Coir Industry Act, However, since 1986, every Bye-law made under the Act will have to be laid before each House of Parliament as contemplated
in Section 27 (4). Records are being collected to confirm and get the dates of placement of these Bye-laws o the Table of both the Houses of
Parliament.
2. Point referred- Bye-laws 3-Application
These Bye-laws shall apply to every employee of the Board, but shall not apply to:
a. any person in casual employment;
 
b. any person on daily wages:
c. any person subject to discharge from service on less than one months notice;
2. Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (1) the Central Government may by order exclude from the operation of all or any of these
Bye-laws any class of employees of the Board.
3. If any doubt arises as to whether these Bye-laws or any of them apply to any person, the matter shall be forwarded to the Central
Government who shall decide the same.
The non-applicability of bye-laws to any person subject to discharge from service on less than one months notice; as prescribed in bye-laws (c)
above, excluding from the operation of all or any of these bye-laws any class of employees of the Board, mentioned in sub bye-law (2) above and in
case of doubt, as to whether the bye laws or any of them apply to any person, the matter shall be referred to the Central Government who shall
decide as contained in sub bye-law (3) above give a contention to a reader that bye-laws do not apply in general and discriminate among its
employees. Why don’t the Board abolish all the three sub-bye-laws?
Is there any objection to make applicability of bye-laws crystal clear by the Ministry as envisaged in the Central Civil Services (Classification,
Control & Appeal) Rules, 1957 (now 1965) for the persons to whom they will be applicable?

There is no discrimination amongst the employees of the Board. The disciplinary proceedings as applicable to regular employees are not applicable
to the Casual employees, daily wagers etc. even under CCS (CCA) Rules. However, the Board will be guided by the recommendations of this
Committee on Subordinate Legislation.

REPRESENTATIVE OF MINISTRY OF INDUSTRY
Shri Satpal, Director
At the outset, the Chairman of the Committee welcomed the representatives of the Coir Board and Ministry of Industry and gave a brief account of
the Committee, the objective of the visit and introduction of members of the Committee. Thereafter, the Chairman, Coir Board gave a presentation
about the functions and activities of the Coir Board. The Chairman, Coir Board gave a basic idea about how Coir is extracted from Coconut and
used for various purposes. He informed that the Coir Industry is a agricultural rural based small sector industry employing around five lacs odd
workers out of which 85% were women. He further informed that Coir was a eco- friendly export oriented biodegradable product and is therefore,
in great demand. The Committee was also informed that there was immense potential in the Coir Industry and at present only 30% of the raw
material was being used in it. The progress in the Coir Industry has been rather slow because of the slow pace of modernization. It was also
informed that to prevent unhealthy competition and exploitation export of Coir had been allowed only with the permission of the Coir Board. The

Question No. 1 Whether the rules have been laid on the table of each house of Parliament? If so the details in this regard.
Comments Section 25 (3) of the Rubber Act 1947 (XXIV) of 1947 prescribes that every rule made on matters listed under Section 25 of the Act
shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made before each house of Parliament. The Rubber Board (Service) Rules, 1961 were made in the year
1961 and published on 23rd May, 1961. Records of that period are not available.
Question No. 2 Rule 2 (c)
‘Board’s employee’ means any person employed under the Board other than the Chairman, the Officers appointed under Section 6A of the Rubber
Act, 1947 and the Government Officers lent to the Board.
Why the Chairman and the Officers appointed under Section 6A of the Rubber Act are not treated as Board employee? Kindly explain.
Comments Rule 2 (c) of the Rubber Board (Service) Rules, 1961 are applicable to employees of the Rubber Board excepting for the Chairman and
Officers mentioned in Section 6A of the Rubber Act. There is specific provision in the Rubber Act and Rubber Rules with regard to the appointment
of the Chairman and the Executive Officers appointed under Section 6A.

Rubber Act and Rubber Rules.
The Executive Officers appointed under 6A of the Rubber Act are Rubber production Commissioner and the Secretary. Their terms of appointment
and functions are also specified in the Rubber Act and Rubber Rules. The Central Government makes appointments to these posts. In respect of
Rubber Production Commissioner and Secretary the Government usually stipulates that the terms and conditions of the service will be on par with
the employees of similar grade in the Rubber Board.
Therefore, Chairman and Officers appointed under 6A of the Rubber Act are not governed by the Rubber Board (Service) Rules, 1961.

st April, 1963 and the grant of Pensionary benefits are regulated

Comments –
The Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust Employees (Pay and Allowances) Regulations, 1997 were laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on 27th July, 1998 and
Rajya Sabha on 28th July, 1998.
Question No. 2
Regulation 2(4) "Compensatory Allowance" means an allowance included in the Schedule or approved for inclusion in the Schedule or granted
under these or any other regulations to meet personal expenditure necessitated by the special circumstances in which duty is performed. It includes a
travelling allowance.
What is the justification for including travelling allowance within the meaning of the term "compensatory allowance" when the same has been
defined separately in regulation 2(28).
 
Comments-
The definition as contained in Regulation 2(4) of the JNP Employees (Pay & Allowances) Regulation, 1997 has been borrowed from the definition
of compensatory allowance as contained in the 9(5). This definition of compensatory allowance as contained in the Fundamental Rules specifically
states that it includes travelling allowance. In Regulation 2(28) of the JNP Regulations, travelling allowance has been separately defined as an
allowance granted to the employee to cover the expenditure which he incurs on travelling in the course of his employment and it includes allowance
granted for maintenance of any mode of conveyance. It may be seen that there is no duplication between Regulation 2(28) and Regulation 2(4)
which states that travelling allowance can also be treated as compensatory allowance.
Question No. 3
Regulation 2(19)- "Personal pay" means additional pay granted to an employee –
(i) to save him from a loss of substantive pay in respect of a permanent post due to revision of pay or to any reduction of such substantive pay
otherwise than as a disciplinary measure; or
(ii) in exceptional circumstances, on other personal consideration in accordance with the general orders issued by the Government as the case may
be.
The words "exceptional circumstances, on other personal consideration" appearing in the regulation does not appear to be specific. What are the
circumstances or personal consideration contemplated by the Ministry in this regulation. Whether there is any objection in making the regulation
specific and precise?
Comments-
Government has issued instructions for grant of a special increment in the form of personal pay in respect of employees who undergo sterilisation
operation after having 2 or 3 surviving children. Such personal pay should not be absorbed in further increases in pay either in the same post or on
promotion to a higher post. Such personal pay is also granted for passing certain specified Hindi examinations. It may not be advisable to elaborate
the words ‘exceptional circumstances on other personal consideration’ as it may not be possible to envisage all circumstances when Government
may issue instructions on granting of such personal pay in future. It is however, assured that there is not scope for misuse of this provisions, as such
personal pay can be granted only in accordance with the general orders issued by the government.
Question No. 4
Regulation 4 - Fixation of initial pay-
(I) The initial pay of an employee who is appointed to a post in the Board’s service on a time-scale of pay in regulated as follows:
(a)(i) Where an employee holding a post in a substantive, temporary or officiating capacity in the Board’s service in appointed in substantive,
temporary or officiating capacity as the case may be, subject to the fulfillment of the eligibility conditions as prescribed in the relevant Recruitment
Rules, to another post carrying duties an responsibilities of greater importance than those attaching to the post held by him, his initial pay in the
time-scale of the higher post shall be fixed at the stage next above the notional pay arrived at by increasing his pay in respect of the lower post held
by him regularly by an increment at the stage at which such pay has accrued or rupees twenty five only, whichever is more. Save incases of
appointment on deputation or foreign service to an ex-cadre post, or to a post on ad-hoc basis, the employee shall have

the option, to be exercised within one month from the date of appointment, to have the pay fixed under this regulation from the date of appointment

What is the justification for ensuring a minimum increase of Rs.25/- to an employee of the Port Trust while fixing his initial pay on initial

Rs.25 has been borrowed from Fundamental Rule 22 applicable to Central Govt. employees. This limit has been fixed to ensure certain minimum

Regulation No.24 (2) (ii) is repetition of the conditions already prescribed under Regulation 24 (2) (i) what is the justification for adding Regulation

Comments-
Regulation 24 (2) (i) says that subsistence allowance shall not be made unless the employee furnishes a certificate that he is not engaged in any
other employment, business, profession or vocation. Sub Clause (ii) of this sub regulation states that subsistence allowance shall not be denied on

Question No.9-
Regulation 27(2)
Notwithstanding anything contained in Regulation 24 where an employee under suspension dies before the disciplinary or the Court proceedings
instituted against him are concluded, the period between the date of suspension and the date of death shall be treated as a period spent on duty for all
purposes and his family shall be paid the full pay, and allowances for that period to which he would have been entitled had he not been suspended,
subject to adjustment in respect of subsistence allowance already paid.
What is the justification in allowing the period between the date of suspension and the date of death of an suspended employee as period spent on
duty and allowing the benefits for all purposes?
Comments-
An employee may be suspended pending departmental enquiry or judicial proceedings. On conclusion of departmental enquiry or judicial
proceedings, suspension period is treated is duty, leave or no duty depending on the fact whether the employee was found guilty or not. If an
employee dies before conclusion of departmental enquiry or judicial proceedings such a conclusion cannot be made and therefore the suspension
period is treated as on duty as if he is not guilty. This provision is made to meet the principles of natural justice.

6.12 Rule 12
"Meetings of Board:- There shall be not less than two ordinary meetings of the Board in a year on such dates and at such places as
the Chairman may think fit and the interval between any two ordinary meetings shall not, in any case, be longer than eight months".
The term "such places" appearing in Rule gives arbitrary powers to the Chairman. The Committee felt that in case the meeting of the Board is to be
held outside the Headquarters, the reasons for the same be recorded in writing and the Rule be amended accordingly.
The Committee was informed that this provision lends certain amount of flexibility to convince Board meeting at different places since tobacco is
grown in different States of India. Government have no objection if an amendment is proposed to the Rule to the effect that the reason for holding
the meeting outside the Head Quarters may be recorded in writing.
The Committee dropped its recommendations and decided not to insist for amendment.
13. Rule 13(2)
 
  
  
 
"The Chairman may require any officer of the Board, besides the Executive Director or invite any person to attend any meeting of
the Board, but such officer or person shall not be entitled to vote."
The term "any person" appearing in rule is not clear. The Committee sought to know whether the Ministry have any objection to
specify that persons(s) related to Tobacco Industry may be invited to attend the meeting of the Board and to amend the Rule
accordingly.
The Ministry replied that sometimes the Board may require the assistance/guidance from persons other than those associated directly
with Tobacco Industry for taking policy decisions/corrective measures depending on the nature of the issue. Hence, it may be
appropriate to retain this provision.
The Committee noted the reply.
14. Rule 17
"Voting: (1) Every question brought before a meeting of the Board shall be decided by a majority of the members present and voting.
(2) In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairman or the Vice-Chairman or Members presiding over the meeting of the Board is against
the democratic norms of the modern society. The Committee sought to know whether there is any objection to delete the same?
The Ministry replied that the provision needs to be retained as it would be useful in cases of dead-lock when a resolution is put to vote. Similar
provisions are available in case of other local bodies.
The Committee noted the reply.
 
 
6.15 Rule 18
"Transaction of business by circulation:- (1) Any business which is to be transacted by the Board may, if the Chairman so directs, be
referred to Members (Other than Members who are not in India) by circulation of papers, and copies of papers so circulated shall
also be sent to the Central Government.
(2) Any proposal or resolution circulated under sub rule(1) and approved by the majority of the members who have recorded their

COM
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/126rep.htm[25-10-2016 16:35:12]
views in writing shall be as effectual and binding as if such proposal or resolution was decided by the majority of the members at a
meeting of the Board.
Provided that at least eight members of the Board have recorded their views on the proposal or resolution. Provided further that
when a proposal or resolution is referred to the members by circulation, any five members may require that the proposal or
resolution be referred to members at a meeting and there upon such reference shall be made to members at a meeting of the Board. 
  
 
(3) Where any business is referred to members under sub-rule (1), a period of not less than ten clear days shall be allowed for the
receipt of replies from members and such period shall be reckoned from the date on which the notice of business is issued.
(4) If a proposal or resolution is circulated under this rule, the result of the circulation shall be communicated to all the members and
to the Central Government.
(5) All decisions on questions arrived at by circulation of papers shall be placed at the next meeting of the Board for record.
The Committee sought to know whether Government have any objection in laying down some restrictions/guidelines to curb the temptation to
resort to passing of resolutions by circulation? It is felt that both in law and in practice, a body in its duty constitute meeting constitutes a collective
personality distinct from the individual constituents. In cases of similar provision in other rules, the Committee emphasised that this practice should
be resorted to in special cases only and for reasons to be recorded in writing.
The Ministry replied that on some occasions it may be required to refer to the Board a Report or some additional information sought for during a
recently concluded meeting or a routine matter for which convening a regular meeting may be cumbersome or may not be required or may not be
convenient for a member to attend.
Moreover, the second proviso to Rule18(2) provides that when any business in circulated for approval of Board Members, any five members can
require/insist that the matter be placed before the members in a meeting of the Board. This itself is built-in restrictive provision against
indiscriminate use of this provision. Even otherwise, a resolution passed by circulation shall have to be placed at the next meeting of the Board.
In view of the position explained above, it would be appropriate to retain the provision.
The Committee accepted the reply of the Ministry.
The discussion ended with the mutual vote of thanks.

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

"Provided that a member appointed under clauses(a), (b), (c) and (d) of sub-section (4) of section 4 shall not be eligible for reappointment
for more than two terms and a member appointed under clause (e) shall not be eligible for reappointment for more than one term"

THE ENVIRONMENT (PROTECTION) RULE, 1986-IMPLEMENTATION OF 102ND REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE.
The Committee examined the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986 framed in exercise of powers under sections 6 and 25 of the
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and its recommendation, as re-produced below, were included in its 102nd Report which was presented
to the house on May, 1994:-
"6.12. However, the Committee recommends that powers under section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 should be delegated to
the State Government of Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh without further delay".
2. Extracts from the Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Environment & Forests on May 16, 1994 for implementation of the
recommendations of the Committee.
3. The matter of implementation of the above recommendation of the Committee was perused with the Ministry of Environment & Forests
and the Ministry ultimately published a Notification. SO 609(E) dated July 20, 1998 delegating power under section 5 of the Environment
(Protection) Act, 1986 to the State Government of Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland (Appendix).
4. The Committee at its meeting held on May 20, 1999 considered the matter. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of
Environment & Forests has implemented the recommendation as contained in its 102nd Report regarding delegation of powers to
the State Government of Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh under Section 5 of the Act.

INTRODUCTION
 
 
        I,      the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf,
do hereby present this Hundred and  Thirty Second  Report of the Committee
.
1.2   The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on February 7, 2001.
 
1.3     The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha during its 191st session have been perused by the
Committee in the light of the provisions of the Act under which they have been framed and also with a view to see whether they have been laid
timely and properly. The recommendations of the  Committee in this behalf are contained in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
 
 
NEW DELHI;                                                                                                                              DIPANKAR   MUKHERJEE
February 7,  2001                                                                                                                                                  Chairman,
Committee on Subordinate Legislation,
               Rajya Sabha
  
REPORT
I
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of the Rajya Sabha
(191st Session)
        During the 191 st Session of  the Rajya Sabha, 205 Statutory Orders were laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha by the various
Ministries/Departments.  The details of the Gazette  Notifications in which these were published and the date of their laying on the Table of the
Rajya Sabha have been  indicated in the enclosed statement Ministrywise (Annexure).  Out of these 205 Orders, the Committee has identified six for
detailed scrutiny.  The Orders so identified  have been indicated in the statement.
 
2.
        During the course of general scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has come across several cases where there has been a considerable
time lag between the date of  notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The statement as at Annexure contains a specific mention of the
period of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the Committee’s guidelines.  In many cases the delay is abnormal.  The
observations/recommendations of the Committee in this behalf are contained in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
        3.     The Committee is constrained to note that the Ministry of Finance has taken an unduly long time in laying a large number of regulations
(Sl. nos 32-52 of the Annexure) issued under the Foreign Exchange and Management  Act, 1999 that too without any delay statements. As may be
seen, all these notifications were published in the Gazette  in the first half  of May, 2000 and the Ministry of Finance could have laid these
notifications in the Monsoon Session of  the Rajya Sabha,  which was there  from July 24 to August 25, 2000.  Similarly, there has been a delay in
laying of the regulations at Sl. Nos.  53, 54, 55, 66 and 71 of the Annexure concerning Nationalized  Banks  which  were  also  laid  without  any 
delay  statements. 
 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Finance should avoid such delays in laying of such statutory orders before the
Parliament. 
 
4.
        In case of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Committee regrets to note that there has been an unusually long delay ranging from  one year
to five years nine months in laying of Statutory Orders (Sl. No.107-111 of the Annexure) pertaining to Union Territories of Daman & Diu and
Andaman & Nicobar Islands issued under  the Regulations framed in exercise of powers conferred under Article  240  of the Constitution  of India. 
The Committee has  taken  a  serious  note  of this delay and also the fact that the Ministry of  Home Affairs  have not appended any statement
giving reasons for delay  while laying  these Statutory Orders.  The Committee would like the Ministry of Home Affairs to avoid recurrence of such
instances for future.
                       5.     Similarly,  The Ministry of Rural Development have also delayed the laying  of Statutory Orders (Sl. 166-168 of the Annexure)
concerning Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu issued under Regulations framed in exercise of powers conferred by Article 240 of the

132
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/132nd.htm[25-10-2016 16:37:09]
Constitution.  In this case also, the delay is even greater ranging from four years seventeen  days to five years ten months. The Ministry of Rural
Development have also not appended any delay statement while laying of these Statutory Orders.  The Committee takes a serious note of these
cases of extreme delay in laying of Statutory Orders before the Parliament.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Rural Development would
take due precaution to avoid recurrence of such instances.
               
        6.     The Committee would like to impress upon all the Ministries/Departments to avoid delay in  the laying of Statutory Orders before
Parliament. With a view to ensure  this  the  Committee  reiterates  its
observation made in its 131
st Report that Orders framed under any Central Act, should be laid on the Table of the House in compliance with the
provisions of the Act on the first available opportunity. The Committee further reiterates its following recommendation as contained in the said
report which lay down the time schedule  for the Ministry/Departments of Government of India in the matter of laying of Statutory Orders:-
 
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the
date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is  in Session, on the date of the  publication of  the Order,
during its continuance and in case the time  lag  between  the  date  of  publication  and  the  date  of  the
 
closing  of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session.  All the
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.”
 
7.
        While scrutinizing  the Orders the Committee also examined the aspect whether the original orders that have been laid during the Session
have been framed under the appropriate authority of the concerned Act.  The Committee notes with satisfaction that these Orders have been framed
within the parameters prescribed under the relevant Acts.

Report
 
I
 
Ministry of Finance Notification S.O. No. 995(E) dated 3rd November, 2000 regarding approval of GIC as Indian
Reinsurer under section 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938-Implementation of 134th Report of the Committee on
Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha.
 
      The Committee in its 134th Report presented to the House on 25th April, 2001 inter-alia dealt with the matter relating to Notification S. O. No.
995 (E) dated 3rd November 2000 issued by the Ministry of Finance (Annexure I) which had effect of restricting activities of the GIC in the area of
reinsurance only without formally amending the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Act, 1972.  The Committee after examining the
subject matter observed as follows:
 
“that issue of notification S.O. 995(E) dated 3rd November 2000 which has the effect of restricting the activates of
GIC to the area of reinsurance, without   formally amending the parent Act was not a well considered course of
action on the part of the Ministry of Finance. In Committee’s views, the reasons advanced by the Ministry of
Finance that it is a requirement of law and the IRDA was insisting upon the issue are not convincing enough for
action in such a manner by the Ministry. The Committee is of the view that issue of notification before formally
amending the parent Act was putting the cart before the horse. The Committee also observed that the objectives of
Bill to entrust the task of Indian reinsurer to General Insurance Corporation and delink General Insurance
Corporation from its subsidiaries by carrying out necessary amendments in the GIBN Act 1972 as mentioned in the
Statement of Objects and Reason have already been brought into effect by the Ministry through the notification
followed by the administrative instructions of November 7, 2000. The effect of the notification was to take

140
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/140th.htm[25-10-2016 16:41:14]
advantage of a loophole in the Act to nullify the basic provisions of the Act, and in the Committee’s opinion  the 
action   and  the manner  in  which   it was  achieved constitutes an attempt to bypass the authority of Parliament.
That   this   was  realized   by   the   Ministry   is   clear  from  the subsequent introduction of a Bill on the same subject. The
Committee strongly deprecates the entire episode and trusts that Government will ensure that cases of this kind do not occur in future”.
 
2.     The fact that the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Amendment Bill 2001 which was  introduced in the
Lok Sabha on 12.03.2001 was still pending gave an  impression as if the change in the role of GIC was being managed
by way of executive action or Administrative Instructions (Annexure II) without the authority of the Parliament.
Accordingly, the Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on Nov. 22, 2001 and as desired, the
Ministry of Finance was requested to furnish information as follows:
 “that the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha considered the subject matter in its meeting. While
the Committee noted that the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Amendment Bill, 2001 which was
introduced in the Lok Sabha on the 12
th March 2001 is still pending, it desired to know precisely its present status
along with the present status with regard to the implementation of Ministry’s notification dated the 3 rd November
2000 approving GIC of India as the “Indian Reinsurer” as well as the instructions contained in their D.O. No.
8/27/200-Ins. VI dated 7.11.2000 addressed to the Chairman, GIC.”
 3.     In response, the Ministry of Finance (Insurance Division) vide  their O.M. dated December 3, 2001 furnished the
following:
 (i)       General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Bill, 2000 has been referred to the Standing Committee of Finance on 27 th August, 2001.  The
Bill is pending with the Standing Committee.  The Committee has already held a meeting with Associations and Unions of Insurance Companies.
(ii)     So far 16 insurance companies have been given certificate of registration by Insurance Regulatory & Development Authority.  All the
insurers are required to reinsure their business upto a certain percentage with GIC on its approval as Indian Reinsure on 3.11.2000.
 (iii)    After approval of GIC as the “Indian Re-insurer” four public sector general   insurance   companies   have  
been  given  operational  and functional autonomy on personnel, investment and re-insurance matters through an
administrative order on 7.1..2000.
              (iv)   To handle the co-ordination matter which was earlier handled by GIC a voluntary association of four public
sector general insurance companies namely General Insurers’ (Public Sector) Association of India has been
formed on the basis of recommendation of the Poddar Committee.
         (v)   GIPSA is a voluntary association of public sector general insurance companies.  Apart from co-ordination
matter, common problems concerns and issues of the four companies are discussed and debated in GIPSA forum for
a common approach.
 
4.     The Committee, not being satisfied with the information furnished by the Ministry of Finance, decided to hear their
representatives with a view to seek further clarifications/elucidations on the subject. Accordingly, the representatives of
the Ministry of Finance along with the representatives of the GIC appeared before the Committee on December 20,
2001. During the course of the oral evidence, the Committee desired to know the present status of the Notification dated
the 3rd November 2000 when the General Insurance Business Nationalization (Amendment) Bill, 2001 was still pending
with the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance. The Committee also wanted to know from
the representatives whether the amendment in the General Insurance Business Nationalization Act, 1972 was still
necessary or the Notification issued by the Ministry was enough and if the amendment in the Act was still necessary,
then how did Government issue the Notification. In other words, the Committee wanted a specific reply from the
representatives whether any further amendment of the GIBN Act was called for under the circumstances. The
Committee also wanted confirmation from the Ministry whether the Administrative Instructions dated 7
th November
2000 called for any Legislative backing. In response to the queries from the Committee, the Additional Secretary in-
charge of the Insurance Division in the Ministry of Finance while trying to clarify the position, referred to the enactment
of the Insurance (Regulation and Development) Authority Bill which came  into force with effect  from the 19 th April 
2000. Referring to this
 
Act, he stated that this Legislation had brought about significant changes in the Insurance Act, 1938 as well as the
General Insurance Business Nationalization  Act,  1972.  Earlier,  the  GIC  and  its  four  subsidiaries were
controlling the entire business of General Insurance. The four subsidiaries had the whole field of General Insurance for
competition amongst them. The situation underwent a change with the coming into the force of the IRDA Act which
resulted in opening up of the insurance sector in the private sector. Keeping in view these changes, the GIC which was a
reinsurer only in respect of the four companies had to assume the role of Reinsurer for the private companies also
coming up in the field and hence it was required that GIC be declared as a Reinsurer under section 101A (8)(ii) of the
Insurance Act, 1938. With a view to explain the basis on which Government had issued the Notification dated the 3
rd
November 2000 followed by Administrative Instructions of 7 th November 2000, the representatives stated that as per

140
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/140th.htm[25-10-2016 16:41:14]
the GIBN Act, the Central Government had powers to issue directions and in this context a reference was made to
Section 23 of the GIBN Act which reads out as follows:
 
“The Corporation and every acquiring company shall, in the discharge of its functions, be guided by such directions
in regard to matters of policy involving public interest as the Central Government may give.”
 
5.     The Committee was, however, not satisfied with the explanation furnished by the representatives of the Ministry of
Finance with regard to the basis on which they had issued the Notification as well as the Administrative Instructions
dated the 3rd and 7th November, 2000, respectively. The Committee’s feeling was that the action taken by Government
through the said Notification and the Administrative Instructions ran contrary to the provisions of the General Insurance
Business Nationalization Act, 1972 an amendment to which was still under consideration of the Department Related
Committee on Finance. The representatives of the Ministry agreed to furnish a note clarifying the position. The
Committee also directed the representatives to apprise the Standing Committee on Finance of the recommendations of
COPU as well as this Committee on the subject which is presently ceased of the matter.
 
6.        The Ministry of Finance vide their communication dated 11 th January 2002 furnished their action taken report on the 134 th Report of the
Committee on  the subject  along with  reply to  the observations  made by  the Committee
 
 
during the course of the oral evidence on December 20, 2001. The action taken report as received is enclosed (Annexure
III).
 
7.     The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance has since forwarded the recommendations of
the COPU as well as this Committee (as contained in the 134
th Report) to the Standing Committee on Finance which it
feels would facilitate better consideration of the matter by them.
 
8.        The Committee is not convinced by the comments furnished by the Ministry of Finance with regard to the basis on
which they had issued the Notification dated the 3 rd November 2000 under Section 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act,
1938 as well as the Administrative Instructions dated 7 th November 2000 under Section 23 of the GIBN Act, 1972 with
a view to restrict the activities of GIC to reinsurance business and give operational and functional autonomy to four
subsidiaries in matters relating to reinsurance, investment and personnel. The Committee is not satisfied with the
correlation sought to be established by the Ministry among sections 2(7A)(c), 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938
and sections 25 and 23 of the GIBN Act, 1972 for the purpose of justifying the basis for the issue of the Notification as
well as the Administrative Instructions. The Committee still feels that the action of the Ministry of Finance, Insurance
Division, declaring GIC as the Indian Reinsurer as well as grant of operational and functional autonomy to the
subsidiaries through Administrative Instructions runs contrary to the provisions of the General Business Nationalization
Act, 1972 as it stands at present. This is evident from the perusal of the General Insurance Business Nationalization
(Amendment) Bill, 2001, which is presently under consideration of the Standing Committee on Finance, Section 9(1) of
the General Business Nationalization Act, 1972 contemplates the role of “superintending, controlling and carrying on
business of general insurance” for the GIC which is sought to be changed to “carrying on reinsurance business” through
the said Amendment Bill. The Committee is unable to understand how the change effected in the role of the GIC can get
alongwith the provisions of the GIBN Act, 1972 until the amendment is carried out.The proposed insertion of a new
section 24(A) in the GIBN Act, 1972 whereby the corporation has, on and from the commencement of the General
Insurance Business Nationalization Amendment Act, 2001, been made to cease to carry on general insurance business
also establishes that certain amendments were called for in the GIBN Act before the Government could effect the
changes in
 
the role and function of the GIC. Now, when the General Insurance Business Nationalization (Amendment) Bill, 2001 is
presently under consideration of the Standing Committee on Finance, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of
Finance should not implement their notification dated 3
rd November 2000 as well as the Administrative Instructions
dated 7th November 2000 till the GIBNA Bill as introduced in the Parliament is passed.

Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs
(Insurance Division)

NOTIFICATION
 
New Delhi 3rd November, 2000
 
 
      S.O. 995(E) In exercise of the power vested with the Central Government under Secretion 101A (8)(ii) of the
Insurance Act, 1938, the Central Government hereby approves General Insurance Corporation of India as the “Indian
Reinsurer” to carry on reinsurance business in India.
 
Annexure-II
 
D.O.No.8/27/200-Ins.VI dated 7.11.2000 addressed to Shri D. Sengupta
Chairman, G.I.C. of India from Shri Ajit M. Sharan, Joint Secretary
(INS), Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs.
 
        In has been decided by the Government that the General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC) shall be the “Indian
Re-insurer” under Section 101 (A) (8) (ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938.  This Section provides that-
 
        “Indian re-insurer” means an insurer specified in sub-clause (b) of clause (9)  of Section 2  who carries on
exclusively re-insurance business and is approved in this behalf by the Central Government.”
 
2.     As per requirements of the above Section, GIC will now have to restrict itself exclusively to  re-insurance business
and should cease doing direct insurance business. Presently GIC is carrying on direct business in the areas of  aviation
and crop insurance.  It also supervises and controls the four subsidiary companies in relation to the conduct of general
insurance business GIC may, henceforth, cease underwriting direct aviation and crop insurance business.   These
businesses may now be underwritten by the subsidiary companies in line with the recommendations of the Poddar 
Committee.
 
3.     GIC may take action to implement the other recommendations of the Poddar Committee to give operational and
functional autonomy to the four subsidiary companies in the following areas:
 
·
     Personnel matter
·     Investments
·     Reinsurance
 
4.     A General insurers’ (Public Sector) Association of India (GIPSA) may also be constituted as suggested by the
Poddar Committee to effect coordination among the four subsidiary companies.  This Association may be entrusted with
coordination in the areas of personnel, technical reinsurance, investment and other matters as recommended by the
Poddar Committee.
 
Annexure-II
 
 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation – 134
th Report presented on 25.04.2001

th April, 2001 and observed that issue of notification
S.O. 995(E) dated 3rd November 2000 which has the effect of restricting the activities of GIC to the area of reinsurance,
without formally amending the parent Act was not a well considered course of action on the part of Ministry of
Finance.  In Committee’s view, the reasons advanced by the Ministry of Finance that it is a requirement of law and the

IRDA was insisting upon the issue are not convincing enough for action in such a manner by the Ministry.  The

        Government issued notification dated 3.11.2000 through existing power vested  under section 101A(8)(ii)  of
Insurance  Act 1935.   The  legal position and the circumstances under which the notification issued are given in the

·     Vide notification No.S.O.770 (E) dated 29
th December, 1972 issued under Section 35 of the General Insurance
Business (Nationalisation)  Act, 1972, the concept  of  Indian Re-insurer defined in Section 101 A (8)(ii) of Insurance
Act, 1938 had been modified to mean General  Insurance Corporation (GIC). Thus in nationalized scenario, Indian Re-
insurer meant GIC which was taking care of the reinsurance business of its four subsidiaries.
 
·     With the enactment of Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) Act, 1999, the monopoly of the
nationalized insurance industry ceased and private insurance companies started getting registration from IRDA for
commencing insurance business in India.  GIC, therefore, could not have reinsured the business of private insurance
companies.
 
·     For reinsuring the business of private insurance companies, it was required to be notified as “Indian Reinsurer”
under Section 101A(8)(ii) Insurance Act, 1938.
 
·     Therefore, the notification issued under Section 35 of GIBNA 1972 was rescinded and GIC was approved on

2.     As per Section2(7A)(c) of the Insurance Act, 1938 an “Indian insurance company” can carry on life insurance
business or general insurance business or re-insurance business. Further, Section 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938,

1972, GIC and the subsidiary companies are under obligation to be guided by direction in regard to matters of policy 
involving public interest as the Central Government may give.  Since it was decided as a matter of policy to declare GIC
as the “Indian Re-insurer” and necessary notification issued, keeping in view the above referred legal position,

functional autonomy to four subsidiaries on matters relating to re-insurance, investment and personnel.

companies from GIC to the government.  The  issue of the direction dated 7.11.2000 is only limited to the grant
operational and functional autonomy to four subsidiaries in certain matters.  Further, while the bill was introduced in the
Lok Sabha on 12
th  March, 2001, the groundwork for the introduction of the Bill was done much before the issue of the
notification dated 3.11.2000.  Therefore, the introduction of the Bill was not an subsequent realization but a part of the 
continuum of the procedural requirement.   The chronological developments with regard to the amendment to GIBNA is

REPORT 
I 
The Bank Officer Employees’ (Conduct) Regulations, 
1976- Implementation of the recommendations of the 
Committee as contained in its 124th Report. 
 
 
 The  Bank Officer Employee’s (Conduct) Regulations, 
1976, framed under the Banking Companies(Acquisition and 
Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 were examined by the 
Committee and the matter was reported to the House on April 
23, 1999 in the 124 th Report of the Committee.  The 
observations/recommendations of the Committee as contained 
in the said Report are as under:  
 
“5.    The Committee notes with satisfaction that the 
Ministry of Finance as well as the Banks have accepted 
the recommendations of the Committee in relation to 
Regulations 3(1) and 6(4). 
 
6. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Finance 
as well as the Ban ks based in Calcutta and Chennai 
called for no change in relation to Regulation 3(3). The 
Ministry and the Banks had maintained that having 
regard to the nature of work in the banking Industry 
and in the exigencies of work, it was not always possible 
to give written instructions to the subordinates.  It was, 
therefore, submitted by the Banks that no change is 
called for in this regard.  The Committee considered the 
matter and came to the conclusion that any oral 
direction issued under the regulation should always be 
confirmed in writing and there should be no objection 
to this change in the regulation. 
 

7. With regard to Regulation 6(1) the Committee 
observed that while the Indian Bank, Indian Overseas 
Bank and Allahabad Bank maintained that there was 
no need t o specifically mention in the regulation that 
the competent authority must record the reasons for 
directing an official to discontinue honorary work, the 
Chennai based Indian bank had no objection for 
recording in writing of the reasons if so desired by th e 
Committee.   
8.     With regard to Regulation 22(1) relating to second 
marriage the Committee noted the reply of the Banks 
and decided not to pursue for any change in the 
Regulation. 
 
9.    The Committee noted the views of the Ministry and 
the Banks on R egulations 4, 10 and 22(3) and decided 
that these regulations may remain in their existing 
form. 
 
10.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance 
shall make necessary modifications/amendments in the 
regulations in cases where they have agreed with t he 
Committee’s suggestions and also as per the 
Committee’s recommendations as stated above, in 
relation to regulations 3(3) and 6(1), expeditiously 
under intimation to the Committee”. 
 
2. The above extracts from the Report were forwarded to 
the Ministry of Finance on May 18, 1999 for necessary action. 
 
3. The Ministry vide their O. M. dated December 3, 2001 
furnished a copy of the notification No. OCR/ 1/ 2001 dated 
June 2, 2001 publishing the UCO Bank Officer Employees’ 
(Conduct) Amendment Regulations, 2001 (Ann exure) 

carrying out amendments in regulations 3(1), 3(3), 6(1) and 
6(4) as per the Committee’s recommendations. 
 
4.  The Committee notes with satisfaction that the 
Ministry/ UCO Bank have amended regulation 3(1) by 
substituting the words “bank employee” with the words 
“officer employee”; regulation 3(3) by providing for 
confirmation in writing of oral direction given by the superior 
official; regulation 6(1) providing for  recording of reasons 
while directing an official to discontinue any honorary work of 
social or charitable nature, etc. in view of exigencies of bank 
work ; and regulation 6(4) by substituting the word “fee” by 
the words “payment in the form of fee, remuneration, 
honorarium and the like in cash or kind”. 
 
5. The Committee recommends the Ministry of Finance to 
take necessary action to ensure that all the  nationalised banks 
carry out these amendments in their conduct regulations 
expeditiously with intimation to it.

II 
The Bank (Officer’s) Service Regulations, 1979 - 
Implementation of the recommendations of the 
Committee as contained in its 124th Report. 
 
 
 The Committee in its 124 th Report presented to the 
House on April 23, 1999 ha d inter-alia examined the Bank 
(Officer’s) Service Regulations, 1979 of the Subsidiary Bank 
of State Bank of India, viz the State Bank of Travancore and 
the State Bank of Mysore framed under the State Bank of 
India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959.  The Commit tee in its 
Report had recommended as under: 
 
 (i)  Regulation 50(3) 
 
The Committee had a detailed discussion on the 
provisions of Regulation 50(3).  It was convinced that the 
directions from the superior official under this regulation 
could not always be i n writing.  But, in the opinion of the 
Committee, there should be no objection to the confirmation 
of such oral directions in writing at the earliest available 
opportunity.  The Committee recommends that the regulation 
be amended, accordingly. 
 
(ii)  Regulation 50(4)   
 
The Committee considered the views of the Ministry of 
Finance as well as the views of the State Bank of Mysore on the 
Committee’s suggestion to replace the words “Bank Official” 
by the word “Officer” and recommended that the Committee’s 
suggestion for suitable modification of regulation 50(4) which 
has been accepted by the Ministry of Finance should be acted 
upon and the regulation may be modified suitably. 
 

(iii) Regulation 51(1) 
 
The Committee expresses its satisfaction that the 
representatives of both the Banks have, during the course of 
discussion, agreed to the suggestion of the Committee that the 
reasons for directing a Bank Official to discontinue any work 
of social or charitable nature should be recorded in writing .  
The Committee recommends that the suitable action may be 
taken for amendment of the regulation 51(1). 
(iv) Regulation 51(4) 
 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the 
Ministry of Finance as well as the representatives of the banks 
have agreed to replace the word “fee” by the word “payment” 
which is more appropriate.  It hopes that suitable amendments 
would be carried out expeditiously. 
 
(v) Regulation 54, 64(1) & (2) 
 
The Committee notes the explanation furnished by the 
Ministry of Finance as well as the representatives of the banks 
on Regulations 54, 64(1)and (2) and decides that the 
regulations may remain in their existing form .”

forwarded to the Ministry of Finance on May 18, 1999 for

 “This Ministry has accepted all the recommendations

3. The Ministry of Finance on December 3, 2001

STATE BANK OF TRAVANCORE (OFFICERS’)

 The State Bank of Travancore (Officers’) Service 
Regulations, 1979 were examined and certain points were 
referred to the Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic

their comments.

the State Bank of Travancore and representative of the 
Ministry of Finance at Kochi on the 8 th October, 1993.  The 
points referred to and the comments thereon are enclosed  
(Annexure-I). 
3. The relevant extracts from the study note on the above 
discussions (Annexure-II) were forwarded to the Ministry of 
Finance, (Banking Division) on the 6 th May, 1994 for 
furnishing action taken notes on the 
observations/recommendations of the Committee contained 
therein. 

4. After some reminders the Ministry vide their 
communications dated the 6 th February, 1995 informed as 
under: 
“that recommendations/suggestions contained in the 
study note are being examined in consultation with State 
Bank of Travancore, State Bank of India and Indian Banks’ 
Association.  The comments of this Ministry will be furnished 
to Rajya Sabha Secretariat, as early as possible.” 
Later on, the Ministry of Finance vide their 
communication dated 8 th January, 1996 informed  that  State 
Bank of India had taken up the matter with Reserve Bank of 
India and that a reply from State Bank of India was awaited.  
The Ministry promised to  furnish the information to Rajya 
Sabha Secretariat in due course. 
5.          In the meantime, certain additional points on the above  
Regulations, were culled out and referred to the Ministry on 
the 6 th November, 1996 for their comments. The points 
referred to and the comments received on 14th November, 1996 
are placed at Annexure III. 
6.          The  subject was again discussed with the 
representatives of the State Bank of Travancore  and 
Ministry of Finance at Chennai on November 14, 1996.    A 
study note on the above discussion (Annexure-IV) was  

forwarded to the Ministry  on September 3, 1997 for their 
comments on the points raised therein.  In the absence of  any 
response to the Committee’s above communication, the 
Committee considered the question of delay on the part of the 
Ministry of Finance in responding to the communications on 
its behalf.  The Committee took a serious view in the matter 
and decided to call the Secretary of the Ministry of Finance 
to explain the reasons for inordinate delay in responding to 
its communications.  The Committee’s feelings were 
communicated to the Ministry on the 5th  May, 2000.  As a 
consequence, the Ministry furnished the action  taken note 
vide their communication dated May 30,  2000 enclosed as 
Annexure-V. 
7. The Committee notes Ministry’s comments on para -3 
regarding deletion of provisions of Chapter –III; para -3.1 
regarding powers of the competent authority to decide about 
the period of probation  (Regulation -15); Para-3.5  regarding 
definition of ‘family’ (Regulation 3(h); paras -3.7 and 3.8 
(Regulation 30(2), and para -3.9 (Regulation -29).  The 
Committee is satisfi ed that the Ministry have agreed to the 
Committee’s suggestion to incorporate Government’s 
guidelines with regard to raising retirement age from 58 to 60 
years in the regulations of the State Bank of  India as well as 

all the Associate Banks.  The Committe e further notes with 
satisfaction that the Ministry have agreed to incorporate a new 
sub-clause in Regulation 3(1) defining the term “perquisites’ 
in respect of the State Bank of India Officer’s Service 
Regulations and the Officer’s Service Regulations of 
subsidiary banks of the State Bank of India.  The Committee 
is also happy to note that the Ministry have agreed to amend 
provisions of regulation -38 regarding lapse of leave, after 
death of the employee or when he ceases to be in the service  of 
the bank, suitably as there was some ambiguity in its wording. 
8. The Committee however expresses its unhappiness 
over the long delay on the part of the Ministry of Finance in 
taking action on Committees recommendations and 
responding to communications on its behalf.  It, however, 
hopes that the Ministry would be more responsive in future 
and would carry out the necessary amendments in the State 
Bank of Travancore (Officer’s) Service Regulation, 1979 by 
notifying the same expeditiously under intimation to it.

3. Point referred 
 Regulation 13: Proviso 
  
Provided that the Executive Committee may of its own 
motion review any such decision and where it reviews any such 
decision, it shall give an opportunity to the officer conc erned 
to make his representation in the matter. 
 
i) What is the criteria for reviewing the decision of 
the Committee by the Executive Committee?  Whether it is 
done regularly or in exceptional cases? 
 
ii) Clause (3) of regulation 13 states that the 
decision of the Committee shall be final, whereas the proviso 
to clause (3) empowers the Executive Committee to review the 
decision of the Committee.  There appears to be contradiction.  
Please elucidate. 
 
Comments  of the Bank 
 
i) The decision, if any, given by the Committee is 
not in consonance with the principles of natural justice, such 
matters if brought to the notice of the Executive Committee by 
the Bank the Executive Committee can review the decision of 

the C ommittee appointed for redressal of anomalies.  
However,  there was no occasion to review the decisions  of the 
Committee, as the cases of anomalies brought to the notice of 
the Committee were taken up with State Bank of India, 
Central Office who in turn h ad taken up with appropriate 
authorities viz., IBA and as per the clarification given by them 
the fitment appeal have been disposed off. 
 
ii) As far as the aggrieved officer is concerned, the 
decision of the Committee is final and he cannot appeal to 
Executive Committee for review of the decision of the 
Committee. However, the Executive Committee, suo motto can 
review the decision of the Committee and in such a review shall 
give an opportunity to the officer to represent his case.  In a 
limited sense, we may sa y, the decision of the Committee is 
subject to review by the Executive Committee. 
 
4. Point referred 
Regulation 15                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
 
(3) Any other person appointed to any gr ade including 
Junior Management Grade shall be on probation for such 
period as may be decided by the competent authority. 
 
Provided that the competent authority may, in the case 
of any officer, reduce or dispense with the  period of 
probation. 
 
  This regulation gives blanket power to competent 
authority to decide the period of probation, which might be 
misused.  Whether the Ministry have issued any  guidelines 
to the competent authority?  If so, the details thereof? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 

 This is  only an enabling provision, to equip the 
competent authority with the powers to reduce or dispense 
with the period of probation, in case of direct appointment in 
senior position, where such probation period of longer 
duration may not be required by virtue  of his experience in 
discharging similar duties.  However, in practice, the authority 
conferred under this regulation is not exercised.  As a part of 
promotional policies every officer is kept on one year 
probation on promotion from one grade to another right upto 
scale VII.  In this connection, no guidelines have been received 
from the Ministry. 
 
 
4.1 Point referred  
Regulation 15: Proviso 
 
This proviso creates disparity among the Bank  Officers 
and directly affects the spirit of equality under article 14 of the 
Indian Constitution.  Whether the Ministry have any objection 
to specify the conditions under which the probation period of 
a particular officer will be reduced or dispensed with? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 
  Probationary Officers who are entering the  Bank’s  
service for the first time have to be adequately trained 
before they are entrusted with responsible assignments.  
Similarly Trainee Officers (Group  B Officers)  considering 
their limited exposure to various spheres of banking 
activity are also pu t under training for a   period of one 
year.  Taking into account the nature of appointment of 
these category of officers, the probation period has been  
prescribed as two years as against one year for other 
promoted officers.  Even though probation period  has  
prescribed  as two years and one year for probationary 

officers, Trainee Officers and one year for other  
promotees respectively  for all purposes viz., increment, 
seniority, and promotion it is their date of 
appointment/date of promotion which are t aken into 
account and not the date of confirmation,  for determining 
their consequential benefits.  Therefore, fixation of 
different probation period for different category of officers 
is related to needs of training/job requirements and does 
not amount to  violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. 
 
5. Point referred 
       Regulation 19 
 
(1) An officer shall retire from the service of the  Bank on 
attaining the age of fifty eight years or upon the completion of 
thirty years’ service whichever occurs first. 
 
Provided that the Competent Authority may, at its 
discretion extend the  period of service of an officer who has 
attained the age of fifty eight years or has completed thirty 
years’ service as the case may be, should such extension be 
deemed desirable in the interest of the Bank. 
 
Provided further that an officer who had joined the 
service of the Bank either as an officer or otherwise on or after 
the 19th July, 1969 and attained the age of 58 years shall not be 
granted any  further extension in service. 
 
Provided further that an officer may, at the discretion 
of the Executive Committee, be retired from the Bank’s service 
after he has attained 50 years of age or has completed 25 years’ 
service, as the case may be, by giving him three months’ notice 
in writing or pay in lieu thereof. 
 

Provided further that an officer who has completed  25 
years’ service may be permitted by the Executive Committee 
to retire from the Bank’s service, subject to his giving three 
months notice in writing or pay in lieu thereof unl ess this 
requirement is wholly or partly waived. 
 
Under what circumstances an officer may be 
compulsorily retired?  Whether, principles of natural justice 
is followed in doing so? 
 
Comments  of the Bank 
 
  This regulation in principle provides an opportunity to 
review service records and performance of an officer based 
upon which the extension in his service could be considered 
on completing 25 years of service or attaining 50 years of 
age.  However, in practice first such review is being made 
only on attai ning 50 years of age or   on completion of 30 
years of service whichever is earlier in case of those joined 
the services of the Bank after 19.7.69 and 55 years of age 
or 30 years of service whichever is earlier in case of those 
joined before 19.7.1969.  Si milarly, second such review is 
being done on attaining 55/58 years of age depending upon 
their date of joining the service of the Bank.  In case the 
service records and performance report of the officer is not 
satisfactory, he will be given an extension fo r a shorter 
period, and also advised to improve upon deficient areas of 
his performance.  Depending upon his subsequent 
performance, further extension will be considered.  The 
very fact that the discretion to retire the officer at the end 
of 25 years of service or on attaining 50 years is vested with 
the Executive Committee, the highest decision making 
body in the Bank who represent various interests including 
those officers and workmen and does so after 
independently applying their minds, ensures that the  

principles of natural justice are upheld.  Further, no courts 
have so far questioned the powers under the  principles of 
natural justice.

3.1 At the outset, Shri K. Ramakrishnan, Managing 
Director of the State Bank of Travancore welcomed the 
Committee and introduced officials of the Bank.  The 
Chairman also introduced the Members and officers of the 
Committee.  Thereafter, Shri Ramakrishnan gave a brief

 The Committee, then, initiated discussion in the light of

3.2 As regards guidelines for the appointment of a 
Committee under proviso to Regulation 7, the Committee was 
informed that a Committee consisting of M.D., G.M. 
(Operations) and G.M. (Planning Development) was 
constituted for hearing appeals and to remedy anomalies 
arising out of the placement of officers in the revised scale.  The 
Committee felt that in the present context the appointed 
committee is of no use and has lost its relevancy.  Therefore, 
the Committee  recommended that the proviso to regulation  
providing for appointment of a Committee, appears to be 
redundant, hence, should be deleted.

Committee noted the reply of the Ministry that the Executive 
Committee can review the decision of the appointed 

Committee in case any error is brought to its notice in the

3.4 As regards regulation 8 (3) the Committee  accepted the

officers for the next increment. 
 
3.5 As regards proviso to regulation 13, the Committee was 
informed that the Executive Committee can review the 
decisions of the appointed committee, when it is of the view 
that the principles of Natural Justice have not been followed.

been taken for review.  As regards the contradiction between 
clause (3) of regulation 13 and proviso thereto the Committee
